headline: Amazon commits $13B to expand AI and cloud infrastructure in India by 2030
summary: This fresh investment boosts Amazon Web Services' data center capacity in Mumbai and Hyderabad, bringing Amazon's total India commitments to $48 billion.
details: Amazon announced a new $13 billion investment to expand its AI and cloud footprint in India through 2030. This commitment will primarily fund the growth of Amazon Web Services' data center capacity in key cities like Mumbai and Hyderabad.

The announcement came after Amazon CEO Andy Jassy met with India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi. This marks Amazon's third significant investment commitment in India in recent years, underscoring the country's growing strategic importance.

With this latest pledge, Amazon's total investment commitments in India now reach $48 billion. This includes previous commitments of $15 billion in 2023 (with $12.7 billion for AWS) and over $35 billion in December 2025.

Amazon's move is part of a broader trend, as global technology companies increasingly view India as a major hub for AI computing infrastructure. Microsoft previously committed $17.5 billion by 2029, and Google announced $15 billion for an AI hub and data center infrastructure.

India has also attracted billions in data center investments from other major players, including Australia’s AirTrunk, Canada Pension Plan Investment Board’s CPP Investments, and domestic conglomerates like Reliance Industries and Adani Group.

New Delhi has actively sought to attract such investments through policy incentives, including tax exemptions for foreign cloud providers. These exemptions apply to services sold overseas but run from Indian data centers.

Beyond cloud infrastructure, Amazon is also expanding its domestic retail and logistics network in India. The company plans to open over 20 fulfillment centers and more than 100 last-mile delivery stations this year.

Amazon is also expanding its quick-commerce service, Amazon Now, to over 300 cities and towns. This puts it in direct competition with established players like Blinkit, Swiggy’s Instamart, Zepto, and Walmart-owned Flipkart in India's crowded market.

headline: Ford hired back former engineers to fix mistakes made by automated systems
summary: Ford's over-reliance on automated systems in design and production led to quality issues and a rise in recalls. The automaker brought back over 350 experienced engineers to retrain systems and mentor staff.
details: Ford recently achieved the No. 1 spot in JD Power’s initial quality ranking for the first time in 16 years. This turnaround comes after significant challenges, primarily stemming from an over-reliance on automated systems in design and production, which led to a drop in vehicle quality.

Charles Poon, VP of vehicle hardware engineering, stated that the company mistakenly believed introducing AI and adjusting design requirements would automatically produce high-quality products. Ford underestimated the value of institutional knowledge held by veteran engineers.

Many experienced personnel left before their knowledge was fully transferred to automated systems. This necessitated rehiring some former employees and bringing back over 350 experienced engineers to retrain AI models, improve data collection, and mentor younger staff.

These issues contributed to Ford leading the industry in recalls and experiencing quality slips over several years. Specific difficulties arose during the launches of the Explorer and Aviator models, compounded by supply-chain disruptions.

COO Kumar Galhotra noted that Ford's quality approach had become too fragmented, relying on a 'find and fix' philosophy. The company is now shifting towards preventing issues before they occur, focusing on early indicators rather than post-production corrections.

The transformation also involves closer collaboration between software, digital, vehicle engineering, manufacturing, and supply-chain teams. Ford aims to combine the speed of software development with the rigorous validation required for automotive-grade engineering.
